newsitem.title: USA: National Fuel Q3 helped by utility segment.
newsitem.headline: National Fuel Q3 helped by utility segment.

text.p: National Fuel Gas Co reported an 9.2 percent increase in third quarter earnings, citing strong performances by its regulated operations during the June quarter.
"Third quarter earnings show strong performances by National Fuel's regulated Utility and Pipeline and Storage segments, Chief Executive Bernard Kennedy said.
"However, the Exploration and Production segment's results reflect softer oil and gas prices and a decrease in production."

In the Utility segment, colder weather, new rates effective in October 1996 within New York and lower operation and maintenance (O&M) expense, were the main contributors to higher earnings, the company said.
O&M expense was down 3.3 percent from the prior year's quarter in large part due to the labor savings from a manpower reduction and the continued emphasis on controlling costs.

In the Pipeline and Storage segment, lower O&M expense and higher revenue from unbundled pipeline sales and open access transportation benefited earnings this quarter as compared with the prior year's third quarter.

In the Exploration and Production segment, earnings declined on a 17 percent decline in oil and gas revenue for the quarter compared with the prior year quarter. There was also a five percent decline in total production to 12.4 billion cubic feet equivalent from 13.1 billion.

National Fuel said the decline in production from the prior year reflects the decline in production of onshore horizontal wells and reduced working interest from Vermilion 252, which resulted from the early payout on that well.
Kennedy described the production decline as "short-term," saying it "is a direct result of the limited availability of drilling rigs due to the renewed interest and activity offshore in the Gulf.

"As a result, to date we have not been able to drill as many wells as we planned and place them on production. The good news to report is that we have obtained the drilling rigs necessary to get our program back on track."
